question.text: Under Regulation 20(11) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012, the appointment of a custodian for a Category I or Category II AIF is:

answer.text: Mandatory for all AIFs — the Sponsor / Manager shall appoint a custodian for safekeeping of the securities of the fund.
Mandatory only if the corpus exceeds ₹500 crore.
Optional for Cat II AIFs and mandatory only for Cat I.
Required only for AIFs that invest in listed securities.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 79 and 194), the Sponsor/Manager of an AIF SHALL appoint a custodian for safekeeping of the securities of the fund. Custodian appointment is mandatory for ALL AIFs, each scheme can have a different custodian, and the appointment must be made prior to the date of first investment of the scheme. The Trap: There is no ₹500 crore corpus threshold for custodian appointment. Custodian is mandatory across Cat I, II and III — not optional for Cat II — and the listed-securities-only carve-out does not appear in the current workbook text. Note: Anchor the answer in the workbook's three plain rules — mandatory, possibly different per scheme, and pre-first-investment — without adding shortlisting timelines.
